title: ‘I longed to play the Bach violin double with my daughter – but then I got MS’

paragraphs.en: At first, I failed to recognise the significance of the deterioration in my violin technique.
paragraphs.zh: 起初，我没有意识到我的小提琴技法退步意味着什么。

paragraphs.en: I was preoccupied by other concerns – the crushing exhaustion that I would describe to my doctors as “not normal tiredness”, the unexplained falls from my bike. I did not draw any connection between these issues and my out-of-tune violin playing. Only when the right side of my body detached itself from my central nervous system to the point where I could no longer pick up a pen or walk without a stick to support myself did the words this feels neurological cross my mind.
paragraphs.zh: 我被其他问题困扰着——那种我会向医生描述为“不正常的疲惫”的压垮人的疲惫感，还有莫名其妙从自行车上摔下来。我没有把这些问题和我走音的小提琴演奏联系起来。直到我身体的右侧从我的中枢神经系统中“脱离”，让我再也无法拿起笔、无法不用拐杖行走时，“这感觉像是神经系统的问题”这句话才掠过我的脑海。

paragraphs.en: By the time the neurologist told me the MRI results, I had self-diagnosed with everything from a brain tumour to stress. The official diagnosis of remitting-relapsing multiple sclerosis was almost a relief. My then eight-year-old daughter was not about to be orphaned. There were disease modifying therapies which would hopefully reduce the number and severity of the attacks.
paragraphs.zh: 等神经科医生把核磁共振结果告诉我时，我已经给自己下了从脑瘤到压力等各种诊断。官方诊断是复发缓解型多发性硬化症（MS），这几乎让我松了一口气。我当时八岁的女儿不会被抛下成为孤儿。还有疾病修正疗法，有望减少发作的次数和严重程度。

paragraphs.en: Eventually the disease went into remission and my body returned to close to its previous condition. I was able to put aside the walking stick (at least between relapses) and resume typing my long overdue PhD thesis. But my balance and my fine motor skills had been permanently eroded. I never rode my bike again. My violin languished in its case.
paragraphs.zh: 最终疾病进入缓解期，我的身体也恢复到接近从前的状态。我能放下拐杖（至少在复发间歇期可以），并重新开始撰写我那篇拖延已久的博士论文。但我的平衡能力和精细运动技能已经永久受损。我再也没骑过自行车。我的小提琴在琴盒里黯然蒙尘。

paragraphs.en: Violin had never been my main occupation, but I could not imagine a life in which there were no more impromptu jam sessions with friends, family and sometimes total strangers. No more playing catchy tunes to entertain young children. No more scraping out a Vivaldi concerto or Handel sonata when I needed to boost my mood. I consoled myself with the knowledge that as much as I loved the instrument I had been playing since I was seven years old, I had only ever been a very ordinary violinist. All the same, the loss still stung.
paragraphs.zh: 小提琴从来不是我的主业，但我无法想象没有它的生活：不再有与朋友、家人、有时甚至与陌生人即兴合奏的时光；不再演奏朗朗上口的曲调逗孩子们开心；不再在需要提振心情时拉上一段维瓦尔第协奏曲或亨德尔奏鸣曲。我只能安慰自己，尽管我深爱这把从七岁起就一直在拉的乐器，但我从来都只是一个非常普通的小提琴手。尽管如此，失去它仍然刺痛了我。

paragraphs.en: Related: Christina Applegate on life with multiple sclerosis: ‘I won’t lie and say any of this is a blessing’
paragraphs.zh: 相关报道：克里斯蒂娜·阿普尔盖特谈多发性硬化症的生活：“我不会撒谎说这一切是福气”

paragraphs.en: As a low-income single mother, I used to busk outside the local shops as my daughter twirled around to the music. Adalya had demanded a violin of her own as soon as she was old enough to hold it and I had looked forward to the day when we would play the Bach double violin concerto together. My friend Althea and I had performed this concerto together in high school, but post-multiple sclerosis, I struggled to play even the easy Mozart duets I had learned in primary school. I had to content myself with watching Adalya’s violin playing from the sidelines.
paragraphs.zh: 作为一个低收入单亲母亲，我过去常常在当地商店门外卖艺，而我的女儿阿达莉娅会随着音乐旋转起舞。阿达莉娅一长大到能握住琴就要求拥有一把自己的小提琴，而我一直盼望着有一天我们能一起演奏巴赫的双小提琴协奏曲。我和朋友阿尔西娅高中时就一起演奏过这首协奏曲，但患上多发性硬化症之后，我连小学时学过的那几首简单的莫扎特二重奏都拉不好了。我只能满足于在场边看阿达莉娅拉琴。

paragraphs.en: I took a long time to accept that my own violin competency was gone for ever. When I eventually passed my violin on to my daughter, I bought a cheap instrument for myself, ready to play once my fine motor skills miraculously returned. One day, I told myself, I will play the Bach double with my daughter, even if it’s just once, even if Bach turns in his grave at my discordant double stops.
paragraphs.zh: 我花了很长时间才接受自己的小提琴能力已经永远消失。当我最终把自己的小提琴传给女儿时，我给自己买了一把便宜的琴，准备等我的精细运动技能奇迹般地恢复后再拉。我告诉自己，总有一天，我会和女儿一起演奏巴赫的双小提琴协奏曲，哪怕只有一次，哪怕巴赫会因为我的双音拉得走调而在坟墓里翻身。
